name: tert-butyl monoperoxymaleate
description: Tert-butyl monoperoxymaleate (CAS 1931-62-0 ) is an organic peroxide used as a radical source in polymer manufacturing and curing systems. It delivers controlled radical generation at moderate temperatures, making it suitable for initiating polymerization. This chemical is effective for cross-linking reactions across multiple substrate types. In plastics and polymer production, it initiates free-radical polymerization of vinyl and acrylic monomers, supporting the manufacture of resins and thermoplastic compounds. Coating formulators use it as a curing agent in unsaturated polyester and acrylic systems where controlled crosslink density affects final film performance. It ensures that the resulting coatings meet specific durability and finish requirements. In adhesive and sealant formulations, it supports room- or elevated-temperature cure schedules for structural bonding applications. This versatility allows manufacturers to tailor their production processes to specific environmental conditions. Elastomer producers apply it as a cross-linking initiator to achieve defined network density in rubber compounds and sealant matrices. This process is critical for maintaining the structural integrity and elasticity of the final rubber products. Tert-butyl monoperoxymaleate is typically supplied as a liquid or solution, often phlegmatized in a plasticizer or solvent to meet transport and handling requirements. This stabilization is necessary for the safe management of organic peroxides. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering, with active oxygen content used as the primary specification parameter. Packaging and concentration levels vary by supplier to comply with regulatory classification thresholds. These standards ensure that the peroxide transport remains safe and efficient across international borders.
